title: RGEN-seq for highly sensitive amplification-free screen of off-target sites of gene editors
boundary: Cas9 cut ends receive a truncated p7L adapter lacking P5; subsequent fragmentation and complementary p5L adapter ligation create cluster-competent P5/P7 molecules. Background P5/P5 molecules are excluded at flowcell clustering. This adapter/physical reporting boundary differs from Digenome whole-genome coverage, SITE-seq affinity capture and CIRCLE/CHANGE circular-template preparations; guide panels and analysis software remain applications.

title: SMASH, a fragmentation and sequencing method for genomic copy number analysis
boundary: Very short genomic fragments are size-enriched, end-processed and ligated into longer chimeric DNA molecules before indexed sequencing-library construction and size selection. Each read samples several independently originating genomic intervals. The physical concatenation preparation, rather than copy-number software, distinguishes it from ordinary WGS and proximity-contact concatemer methods. Same-paper alternative fragmentation/SMASH2 remains one method, not another candidate.

title: Function-based identification of mammalian enhancers using site-specific integration
boundary: Candidate-fragment fluorescent-reporter constructs undergo targeted single-copy integration at the same Hprt locus and drug selection. Reporter-positive cells are physically FACS-enriched, then integrated candidate DNA is amplified and sequenced. This genomic-integration/physical-selection/DNA-recovery route differs from registered transient STARR-seq RNA-output preparation; target loci, differentiated cell types and reporter validation remain one method.
